chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) forbade eating the meat of a camel at the time of its milking.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating camel meat during the time of milking according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes a specific prohibition against consuming camel meat during the state of *ightilam* (freshness or lactation period), tracing the ruling back to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who attributes it to Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). This reflects the Shia emphasis on the continuity of legal authority from the Prophet through the Imams, highlighting practical dietary laws derived from the Ahl al-Bayt's guidance on animal husbandry and ritual purity.
